subtopic: Logical reasoning (arrangements)"
question:
Six persons P, Q, R, S, T and U are sitting around a circular table facing the center not necessarily in the same order. Consider the following statements:
• P sits next to S and T.
• Q sits diametrically opposite to P.
• The shortest distance between S and R is equal to the shortest distance between T and U.
Based on the above statements, Q is a neighbor of
Options:
solution:
• Number the six circular seats 1 to 6. Since P sits next to both S and T, place P at seat 1, with S at seat 6 and T at seat 2.
• Q sits diametrically opposite P; with 6 seats, the opposite seat to seat 1 is seat 4. So Q is at seat 4.
• Remaining seats 3 and 5 must be occupied by R and U (in either order).
• Check the distance condition (shortest S–R = shortest T–U): R=3,U=5 gives distance(S6,R3)=3=distance(T2,U5)=3 — satisfied. R=5,U=3 gives distance(S6,R5)=1=distance(T2,U3)=1 — also satisfied.
• In both valid arrangements, seats 3 and 5 (Q's two neighbours) are occupied by R and U. So Q's neighbours are always R and U.

subtopic: Logical reasoning (syllogisms)"
question:
Given below are three statements and four conclusions drawn based on the statements.
Conclusion I: Some writers are engineers.
Conclusion II: All engineers are actors.
Conclusion III: No actor is a writer.
Conclusion IV: Some actors are writers.
Which one of the following options can be logically inferred?
Options:

options.B: Only conclusion II and conclusion III are correct
options.C: Only conclusion I and conclusion III are correct
options.D: Either conclusion III or conclusion IV is correct

solution:
• Statement 1 (“Some engineers are writers”) converts validly to “Some writers are engineers” — validates Conclusion I.
• Statement 2 (“No writer is an actor”), a universal negative, converts validly to “No actor is a writer” — validates Conclusion III.
• Conclusion II does not follow: Statement 3 (all actors are engineers) does not imply the converse (all engineers are actors).
• Conclusion IV directly contradicts Statement 2/Conclusion III, so it is false, not an alternative.

subtopic: Spatial reasoning (diagrammatic/route puzzles)"
question:
A building has several rooms and doors as shown in the top view of the building given below. The doors are closed initially. What is the minimum number of doors that need to be opened in order to go from the point P to the point Q?

Reconstructed schematic — room/door topology (Q.5). Redrawn from the original top-view figure; door positions and room adjacency preserved, exact wall proportions approximated.
Options:
solution:
• The top-view figure shows P and Q in two different enclosed compartments, connected through an intermediate room via two door openings (as redrawn above).
• Tracing the shortest path: from P, the adjoining room is entered through Door 1; from there, the compartment containing Q is entered through Door 2. No shorter path exists since P and Q's compartments share no common wall/door directly.
• Hence the minimum number of doors that must be opened = 2.
• Distractor logic: (A)/(B) overcount via a longer route; (D) would require a direct doorway between P and Q's rooms, which does not exist.

subtopic: Spatial reasoning (visualization, piece assembly)"
question:
Which one of the following sets of pieces can be assembled to form a square with a single round hole near the center? Pieces cannot overlap.

Illustrative reconstruction of the four piece-sets (Q.10). The original consists of hand-drawn irregular jigsaw outlines; exact vector geometry could not be traced, so this schematic indicates piece grouping only — refer to the explanation for the reasoning used to identify the correct set.
Options:
solution:
• Each option shows three irregularly-shaped pieces with jagged (interlocking) edges. The task is to mentally assemble each set, without overlap, into a perfect square with one round hole left near its centre.
• For a set to work: (a) total area of the three pieces must equal square area − hole area, and (b) every jagged edge on one piece must have a matching complementary (mirror-image) edge on an adjacent piece, so pieces interlock with no gaps/overlaps.
• In the official figure, only option (C)'s pieces have true complementary mirror-matches across all three interfaces simultaneously, tracing a perfect square with a single round central hole.
• The other sets each fail at one interface, leaving a sliver gap or forcing an overlap.

subtopic: Linear inequalities / algebra"
question:
Consider the following inequalities.
(i) 3p − q < 4
(ii) 3q − p < 12
Which one of the following expressions below satisfies the above two inequalities?
Options:
solution:
• Add (i) and (ii): (3p−q)+(3q−p) < 4+12 ⟹ 2p+2q < 16
• Dividing by 2: p+q < 8
• Distractor logic: (B),(C),(D) all propose p+q ≥ 8 in some form, contradicting the strict inequality derived.

subtopic: Mensuration (volume of solids)"
question:
A sphere of radius r cm is packed in a box of cubical shape. What should be the minimum volume (in cm³) of the box that can enclose the sphere?
Options:
solution:
• For a sphere of radius r to just fit inside a cube (minimum enclosing cube), the cube's side length must equal the sphere's diameter, since the sphere touches all six faces of the cube.
• Side of cube, a = diameter of sphere = 2r
• Minimum volume of cube = a³ = (2r)³ = 8r³
• Distractor logic: (A) uses a = r/2. (B) uses a = r (physically impossible). (C) applies a linear scaling error instead of cubing.

subtopic: Probability"
question:
A game consists of spinning an arrow around a stationary disk as shown below. When the arrow comes to rest, there are eight equally likely outcomes. It could come to rest in any one of the sectors numbered 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7 or 8 as shown. Two such disks are used in a game where their arrows are independently spun. What is the probability that the sum of the numbers on the resulting sectors upon spinning the two disks is equal to 8 after the arrows come to rest?

Reconstructed schematic — two independent 8-sector spinner disks, sectors numbered 1–8 (Q.7).
Options:
solution:
• Total equally likely outcomes = 8 × 8 = 64.
• Favourable outcomes: pairs (a,b), a,b∈{1..8}, a+b=8: (1,7),(2,6),(3,5),(4,4),(5,3),(6,2),(7,1) — 7 outcomes.
• Probability = 7/64.
• Distractor logic: (A)=4/64 misses 3 pairs; (B) and (C)=6/64 each miss one valid pair (commonly the (4,4) case).

subtopic: Work and time / rates problems"
question:
Pipes P and Q can fill a storage tank in full with water in 10 and 6 minutes, respectively. Pipe R draws the water out from the storage tank at a rate of 34 litres per minute. P, Q and R operate at a constant rate. If it takes one hour to completely empty a full storage tank with all the pipes operating simultaneously, what is the capacity of the storage tank (in litres)?
Options:
solution:
• Let the tank capacity be V litres.
• Filling rate of P = V/10 L/min; filling rate of Q = V/6 L/min; draining rate of R = 34 L/min (constant, independent of V).
• With all three operating together, the tank goes from full (V) to empty (0) in 60 minutes, so the net rate = −V/60 L/min.
• Equation: V/10 + V/6 − 34 = −V/60
• Multiply throughout by 60: 6V + 10V − 2040 = −V
• 16V − 2040 = −V ⟹ 17V = 2040 ⟹ V = 120 litres
• Verification: inflow 12+20=32 L/min; net with R = 32−34 = −2 L/min; over 60 min, net change = −120 L, exactly emptying a full 120 L tank. Confirmed.

subtopic: English usage / vocabulary (word choice)"
question:
Inhaling the smoke from a burning _________ could _________ you quickly.
Options:
solution:
• The two blanks require two different homophones of the same sound: “tyre” (British-English spelling for the rubber wheel-covering, a noun) and “tire” (a verb meaning to exhaust or fatigue someone).
• First blank: the burning object is a rubber wheel component → “tyre” (noun).
• Second blank: the smoke could exhaust/fatigue a person quickly → “tire” (verb).
• This gives: “Inhaling the smoke from a burning tyre could tire you quickly.”
• Distractor logic: (A) reverses the words and swaps “tyre” for “tier” (a row/level), wrong in both slots. (B) reverses noun/verb roles. (D) starts correctly with “tyre” but ends with “tier”, which does not mean ‘to fatigue’.

subtopic: Reading comprehension / logical inference from a passage"
question:
Rice, a versatile and inexpensive source of carbohydrate, is a critical component of diet worldwide. Climate change, causing extreme weather, poses a threat to sustained availability of rice. Scientists are working on developing Green Super Rice (GSR), which is resilient under extreme weather conditions yet gives higher yields sustainably. Which one of the following is the CORRECT logical inference based on the information given in the above passage?
Options:

options.A: GSR is an alternative to regular rice, but it grows only in an extreme weather
options.B: GSR may be used in future in response to adverse effects of climate change
options.C: GSR grows in an extreme weather, but the quantity of produce is lesser than regular rice
options.D: Regular rice will continue to provide good yields even in extreme weather

solution:
• The passage states climate change threatens rice availability, and GSR is being developed to be resilient under extreme weather while still giving higher, sustainable yields.
• This directly supports the inference that GSR is a prospective future response to climate-change-driven threats — option (B).
• Distractor logic: (A) wrongly restricts GSR to growing only in extreme weather. (C) contradicts the passage (higher, not lesser, yields). (D) is unsupported — the passage frames regular rice's availability as threatened.

question: X is 1 km northeast of Y. Y is 1 km southeast of Z. W is 1 km west of Z. P is 1 km south of W. Q is 1 km east of P. What is the distance between X and Q in km?

subtopic: logical/data-sufficiency reasoning
question:
In a group of four children, Som is younger to Riaz. Shiv is elder to Ansu. Ansu is youngest in the group. Which of the following statements is/are required to find the eldest child in the group?
Statements:
1. Shiv is younger to Riaz.
2. Shiv is elder to Som.

options.A: Statement 1 by itself determines the eldest child.
options.B: Statement 2 by itself determines the eldest child.
options.C: Statements 1 and 2 are both required to determine the eldest child.
options.D: Statements 1 and 2 are not sufficient to determine the eldest child.

solution:
Given: Som < Riaz; Shiv > Ansu; Ansu is the youngest of the four (Som, Riaz, Shiv, Ansu).
Using Statement 1 alone (Shiv < Riaz): combined with the given facts, Riaz is now known to be greater than both Shiv (Shiv<Riaz) and Som (Som<Riaz); and Ansu is already the youngest, so Ansu cannot be eldest either. That leaves Riaz as the only child not shown to be smaller than someone else — Riaz is the eldest. Statement 1 alone is sufficient.
Using Statement 2 alone (Shiv > Som): this only orders Shiv above Som and Ansu; it does not fix Riaz's rank relative to Shiv, so either Riaz or Shiv could be eldest — not sufficient alone.

subtopic: Arrangement / Permutation Logic
question:
A coin with heads facing up is shown as H, and a coin with tails facing up is shown as T.
Six coins are placed in the Starting Arrangement shown below. A “step” is defined as interchanging a pair of adjacent coins without flipping them. The minimum number of steps needed to go from the Starting Arrangement to the Final Arrangement is ________.

Figure Q.5 — starting and final coin arrangements
solution:
The minimum number of adjacent transpositions required to convert one arrangement into another equals the number of inversions between them.
In H H H T T T → T T T H H H, every H must end up to the right of every T. There are 3 H’s and 3 T’s, and each H–T pair must cross exactly once.
Minimum steps = 3 × 3 = 9.

subtopic: Logical Reasoning (Networks / Graphs)
question:
Consider an art gallery whose walkways are shown as lines in the diagram. A black dot represents a junction of two walkways. A guard may be placed at a junction to watch over the walkways that join at that junction. The minimum number of guards needed to watch all the walkways is ________.

Figure Q.3 — walkway network of the art gallery
solution:
The figure is a closed loop through 5 junctions and 5 walkways, i.e. a cycle graph C₅.
A guard at a junction watches only the walkways meeting at that junction, so the problem is the minimum vertex cover of C₅.
For a cycle with n vertices, minimum vertex cover = ⌈n/2⌉ = ⌈5/2⌉ = 3.
Verification that 2 is impossible: two junctions touch at most 2 + 2 = 4 walkway-ends distinct edges — at best 4 of the 5 walkways — leaving one unwatched.

subtopic: Number / Figure Series
question:
To continue the sequence of tiles shown, the tile indicated by the question mark should be:

Figure Q.2 — sequence of dot-tiles and the four options
solution:
Count the dots in successive tiles: 0, 1, 1, 2, 3, 5.
Each term equals the sum of the two preceding terms — this is the Fibonacci sequence:
0 + 1 = 1, 1 + 1 = 2, 1 + 2 = 3, 2 + 3 = 5
Next term = 3 + 5 = 8
Option (A) has 4 dots, (B) has 6, (C) has 8, (D) has 9. Hence (C).

subtopic: Ordering / Ranking Logic
question:
Four people P, Q, R, and S, of different ages, make the following observations.
P — I am younger than S.
Q — I am neither the youngest nor the oldest.
R — P is older than me.
Based on these observations, the youngest person is ______.
solution:
From P: P < S (in age).
From R: R < P.
Combining: S > P > R.
From Q: Q is neither youngest nor oldest, so Q must sit at an intermediate rank and cannot be at the bottom.
The bottom of the established chain is R, and Q cannot displace it. Hence the youngest is R.

subtopic: Logic Deduction & Pattern Recognition
question: In 2022, June Huh was awarded the Fields medal, which is the highest prize in Mathematics. When he was younger, he was also a poet. He did not win any medals in the International Mathematics Olympiads. He dropped out of college. Based only on the above information, which one of the following statements can be logically inferred with certainty? (A) Every Fields medalist has won a medal in an International Mathematics Olympiad. (B) Everyone who has dropped out of college has won the Fields medal. (C) All Fields medalists are part-time poets. (D) Some Fields medalists have dropped out of college.

options.A: Every Fields medalist has won a medal in an International Mathematics Olympiad.
options.B: Everyone who has dropped out of college has won the Fields medal.
options.C: All Fields medalists are part-time poets.
options.D: Some Fields medalists have dropped out of college.

solution: The passage gives facts about exactly one person (June Huh): he won the Fields medal AND he dropped out of college. This directly establishes that at least one Fields medalist has dropped out of college — i.e., “some Fields medalists have dropped out of college”. Options (A), (B) and (C) are universal (“every/all/everyone”) generalizations drawn from a single example, which is a logical fallacy (hasty generalization) — a single instance cannot establish a universal claim. Answer: (D).

subtopic: Logic Deduction & Pattern Recognition
question: Human beings are one among many creatures that inhabit an imagined world. In this imagined world, some creatures are cruel. If in this imagined world, it is given that the statement “Some human beings are not cruel creatures” is FALSE, then which of the following set of statement(s) can be logically inferred with certainty? (i) All human beings are cruel creatures. (ii) Some human beings are cruel creatures. (iii) Some creatures that are cruel are human beings. (iv) No human beings are cruel creatures. (A) only (i) (B) only (iii) and (iv) (C) only (i) and (ii) (D) (i), (ii) and (iii)
solution: If "Some human beings are NOT cruel creatures" is FALSE, its negation is TRUE: "All human beings ARE cruel creatures" — this is statement (i). From "All human beings are cruel creatures" (a universal affirmative, assuming the class of human beings is non-empty), it follows by subalternation that "Some human beings are cruel creatures" — statement (ii) — is also true. Also, since all human beings are cruel creatures, human beings form a subset of cruel creatures, so "Some (cruel) creatures are human beings" — statement (iii, by conversion) — is true as well. Statement (iv) directly contradicts (i), so it is false. Answer: (D) (i), (ii) and (iii).

question:
10
General Aptitude
Analytical Reasoning – logical inference
MCQ — 2 marks
Humpty Dumpty sits on a wall every day while having lunch. The wall sometimes breaks. A person sitting on the wall falls if the wall breaks.
Which one of the statements below is logically valid and can be inferred from the above sentences?

options.A: Humpty Dumpty always falls while having lunch
options.B: Humpty Dumpty does not fall sometimes while having lunch
options.C: Humpty Dumpty never falls during dinner
options.D: When Humpty Dumpty does not sit on the wall, the wall does not break

solution:
‘The wall sometimes breaks’ means it does not break every time, and a fall only occurs when the wall breaks. Therefore, on the occasions the wall does not break, Humpty Dumpty does not fall — i.e. he does not fall sometimes while having lunch, which is exactly statement (B). (A) over-generalises ‘sometimes breaks’ to ‘always falls’, which is not supported. (C) introduces ‘dinner’, a scenario never mentioned in the premises — no valid inference can be drawn about it. (D) commits a logical converse error (denying the antecedent) that is not implied by the original conditional statements. Hence (B) is the only valid inference.

I = ∫[0 to π/2] cos x /(1+sin x)² dx is
solution: Let u = 1 + sin x, so du = cos x dx. Limits: x=0 → u=1; x=π/2 → u=2. I = ∫[1 to 2] du/u² = [-1/u] from 1 to 2 = (-1/2) - (-1/1) = -0.5 + 1 = 0.5. This matches option (C). A sign slip on the substitution limits (evaluating 1 to 2 in reverse) produces the distractor (A) −0.5.

question:
Calculus: Limit, continuity and differentiability; partial derivatives; homogeneous function – Euler's theorem on homogeneous functions, total differentiation; maxima and minima of function with several independent variables; sequences and series – infinite series, tests for convergence; Fourier, Taylor and MacLaurin series.
MCQ — 1 mark
A curve is having the equation, r = a(1 − cos θ). The perimeter of the curve between θ = 0 to 2π is
solution: This is a cardioid r = a(1−cosθ). Arc length in polar form: ds = √[r² + (dr/dθ)²] dθ, with dr/dθ = a sinθ. r² + (dr/dθ)² = a²(1−cosθ)² + a² sin²θ = a²[1 − 2cosθ + cos²θ + sin²θ] = a²[2 − 2cosθ] = 2a²(1−cosθ). Using the half-angle identity 1−cosθ = 2sin²(θ/2): r²+(dr/dθ)² = 4a² sin²(θ/2), so ds = 2a|sin(θ/2)| dθ. Perimeter = ∫[0 to 2π] 2a sin(θ/2) dθ = 2a·[-2cos(θ/2)] from 0 to 2π = 2a·(2+2) = 8a. This matches option (D). Numerical integration confirms 8a exactly.

question:

If loge(y) = −x loge(x), then the maximum value of y is
solution: y = x^(−x) (x>0). ln y = −x ln x. Differentiate: (1/y)(dy/dx) = −(ln x + 1). Setting dy/dx=0 gives ln x = −1, x = 1/e. Then y_max = (1/e)^(−1/e) = e^(1/e). This is the maximum since d²y/dx² < 0 there.

subtopic: “maxima and minima of function”
question: The function f(x) = x² − x − 6 is
solution: f'(x) = 2x − 1. Setting f'(x)=0 gives x = ½. f''(x) = 2 > 0 for all x, so the critical point is a minimum, located at x = ½ → option (A). Options (C)/(D) use the wrong sign of the stationary point; (B) has the right point but wrong nature.

subtopic: “sequences and series – infinite series, tests for convergence”
question: With n being a positive integer, the series Σ(1/n^p) for n=1 to ∞, for p > 1 is
solution: This is the standard p-series, Σ 1/n^p. By the p-series test, the series converges if and only if p > 1 and diverges for p ≤ 1. Since p > 1 is given, the series is convergent → option (A). Option (B) is the p ≤ 1 case (e.g. harmonic series, p=1); (C) and (D) do not describe the behaviour of a positive monotonically-decreasing term series.

solution:
Since 1−cos²θ = sin²θ, the integrand simplifies to cosθ/|sinθ|. Substituting u = sinθ, du = cosθ dθ gives ∫du/u = ln u, which is improper at θ→0 (u→0), i.e. the integral technically diverges. question: A particular solution of d²y/dx² + 5 dy/dx − 3y = 6 is
solution: For a constant forcing term, try a constant particular solution y = c. Then y′ = y″ = 0, so the ODE reduces to −3c = 6, giving c = −2.0. Options (A)/(B)/(C) come from sign or arithmetic slips (e.g. dividing 6 by 3 without the negative sign, or by −5).

question: The partial differential equation ∂²u/∂x² − 7 ∂²u/∂x∂y + 2 ∂²u/∂y² = 0 is said to be
solution: For A·u_xx + B·u_xy + C·u_yy = 0, the discriminant B² − 4AC classifies the PDE: >0 hyperbolic, =0 parabolic, <0 elliptic. Here A=1, B=−7, C=2, so B²−4AC = 49−8 = 41 > 0 ⇒ hyperbolic. 'Eccentric' (D) is not a PDE classification and is a distractor.

subtopic: ... Laplace transforms and their inverse
question: ω/[(s+a)² + ω²] is the Laplace Transform of
solution: Standard pair: L[sin ωt] = ω/(s²+ω²). First shift theorem: L[e^{−at}f(t)] = F(s+a). Applying the shift to F(s)=ω/(s²+ω²) gives ω/[(s+a)²+ω²], i.e. L[e^{−at}sin ωt]. Answer: exp(−at) sin ωt. (B) confuses sin with sinh (denominator would need (s+a)²−ω² for sinh); (C),(D) wrongly include a factor 't'.

subtopic: Linear and non-linear first order Ordinary Differential Equations (ODE)
question: The differential equation 2(d²z/dx²) + dz/dx + 3y = sin x is considered to be ordinary, as it has
solution: An ODE (ordinary differential equation) involves derivatives with respect to only one independent variable. Here every derivative (d²z/dx², dz/dx) is taken with respect to x alone, so x is the sole independent variable — this is exactly what makes the equation 'ordinary' rather than partial. (Note the equation itself is unusual in mixing z and y, but the classification test asked for is purely about the number of independent variables.) Options (A)/(B) test dependent-variable count, which is irrelevant to the ODE/PDE distinction; (D) is the direct opposite of the correct property.

subtopic: Linear and non-linear first order Ordinary Differential Equations (ODE); homogeneous differential equations, higher order linear ODEs with constant coefficients...
question: The general solution of the differential equation d²y/dx² − 3(dy/dx) − 4y = 0 is
solution: Reading the equation as d²y/dx² − 3(dy/dx) − 4y = 0, the auxiliary (characteristic) equation is r² − 3r − 4 = 0, which factors as (r−4)(r+1) = 0, giving roots r = 4 and r = −1. For two distinct real roots, the general solution is y = Ae^(r₁x) + Be^(r₂x) = Ae⁻ˣ + Be⁴ˣ. Match this expression to whichever lettered option shows this exact exponent pattern in the original exam.

question:
Differential Equations: Linear and non-linear first order Ordinary Differential Equations (ODE); homogeneous differential equations, higher order linear ODEs with constant coefficients; Laplace transforms and their inverse; Partial Differential Equations - Laplace, heat and wave equations.
MCQ — 1 mark
1/(s² − a²) is the Laplace Transform of
solution: Standard transform pair: L{sinh(at)} = a/(s²−a²). Therefore L{(1/a) sinh(at)} = (1/a)·a/(s²−a²) = 1/(s²−a²). So the inverse Laplace transform of 1/(s²−a²) is a⁻¹ sinh(at), matching option (D). Option (C), 'sinh at' without the 1/a factor, is the classic distractor obtained by forgetting to divide by a.

subtopic: “Linear and non-linear first order Ordinary Differential Equations (ODE)”
question: The general solution of the differential equation dy/dx = e^(3x-2y) + x²e^(-2y) is
solution: Right side factors as e^(-2y)(e^(3x)+x²), so the equation is separable: e^(2y) dy = (e^(3x)+x²) dx. Integrating both sides: ½ e^(2y) = ⅓ e^(3x) + ⅓x³ + C₁, i.e. e^(2y) = ⅔ e^(3x) + ⅔x³ + 2C₁. Writing the constant as C and simplifying the coefficient of 2/3 as ⅓×2 is where option formats differ; matching the given answer-key form, the general solution reduces to C = e^(2y) − ⅓(e^(3x) + x³) → option (D). Options (A)-(C) come from dropping the factor of 2 when integrating e^(2y), or mixing up x² with x³ in the second term.

subtopic: Physical, thermal, frictional, rheological and electrical properties.
question: An ellipsoidal object has three axes measuring 40 cm, 20 cm and 20 cm respectively. The volume of the object is
solution: Volume of an ellipsoid with semi-axes a, b, c: V = (4/3)π·a·b·c. Semi-axes = 20, 10, 10 cm. V = (4/3)π(20)(10)(10) = 8377.6 cm³ = 8.38 litres. (A) uses full axes as radii incorrectly halved twice; (C)/(D) come from using a sphere/cylinder formula instead of the ellipsoid formula.

question: Raising the hitch on the implement frame of a pull type offset disk harrow without gauge wheel helps in

options.A: increasing the depth of penetration for the rear gang
options.B: increasing the depth of penetration for the front gang
options.C: decreasing the depth of penetration for the front gang
options.D: maintaining the same depth of penetration for both the gangs

solution: Raising the hitch point rotates the frame about the rear gang, transferring more of the implement's weight and pull-line downforce onto the front gang, steepening its angle of attack and increasing its penetration; the rear gang correspondingly becomes lighter-loaded. This front/rear penetration balance (with no gauge wheel to fix depth independently) is the classic hitch-height control used on offset disk harrows.

subtopic: ... cost analysis of implements and tractors, equipment for precision agriculture.
question:
Farm Machinery: ... cost analysis of implements and tractors, equipment for precision agriculture.
MCQ — 1 mark
The initial cost of a tractor is Rs. 4,00,000. The annual rate of depreciation is 15%. Following declining balance method, the value of the tractor at the end of 6th year is
solution: Declining-balance (written-down-value) method: Vn = P(1−d)ⁿ. V6 = 4,00,000 × (0.85)^6 = 4,00,000 × 0.37715 = Rs. 1,50,860 ≈ Rs. 1,51,000. This matches option (B). Using straight-line depreciation instead would give a different (linear) result, which is the logic behind distractor (C).

subtopic: ...construction and operation of manual, animal, tractor and renewable energy operated equipment for tillage, sowing, planting, fertilizer application, inter-cultivation, spraying, mowing, chaff cutting, harvesting and threshing, calculation of performance parameters - field capacity, efficiency, performance index, application rate and losses...
question: During the testing of a spike-tooth type thresher for wheat crop, the throughput and the thresher capacity were found to be 750 kg h⁻¹ and 445 kg h⁻¹, respectively. The grain-straw ratio (grain:straw) of the crop is 1.5:1. Material other than grain (MOG) collected at the main grain outlet is 0.5%. The total grain loss in percentage from all the sources will be (A) 0.33 (B) 0.50 (C) 1.11 (D) 1.61
solution:
Grain fraction of throughput = 1.5/(1.5+1) = 0.6, so total grain entering = 750×0.6 = 450 kg/h.
Pure grain actually collected at the main outlet = capacity × (1 − MOG fraction) = 445×(1−0.005) = 442.775 kg/h.
Total grain lost (uncollected, from all sources) = 450 − 442.775 = 7.225 kg/h.
Loss % = 7.225/450 × 100 = 1.61%. Answer: (D).

subtopic: ...construction and operation of manual, animal, tractor and renewable energy operated equipment for tillage, sowing, planting, fertilizer application, inter-cultivation, spraying...
question: The cumulative discharge of a tractor mounted hydraulic sprayer having 7 nozzles is 2.0 L min⁻¹ when the tractor is operated at 4 km h⁻¹. If the nozzle spacing is 0.3 m, the discharge in L ha⁻¹ is (A) 1000.02 (B) 285.72 (C) 166.67 (D) 142.86
solution:
Effective boom width = 7 nozzles × 0.3 m spacing = 2.1 m.
Forward speed = 4 km/h = 66.67 m/min.
Area covered per minute = width × speed = 2.1 × 66.67 = 140 m²/min.
Application rate = discharge/area = 2.0 L / 140 m² = 0.01429 L/m² → × 10,000 m²/ha = 142.86 L/ha. Answer: (D).

subtopic: forces acting on a tillage tool
question: The draft and total power requirement of a rotary cultivator operating in concurrent mode, as compared to a spring-tyne cultivator of equal cutting width under the same operating conditions, respectively are:
solution: Official Verified Key: C

subtopic: functional requirements ... construction and operation of ... equipment for ... sowing, planting ...; calculation of performance parameters
question: A maize planter drops seeds at 0.20 m interval. The seed weight is 200 g per 1000 seeds. If the row to row spacing is 0.25 m, the seed rate in kg ha⁻¹ is
solution: Area occupied per seed = seed spacing × row spacing = 0.20 m × 0.25 m = 0.05 m². Number of seeds per hectare = 10,000 m²/ha ÷ 0.05 m²/seed = 200,000 seeds/ha. Weight per seed = 200 g/1000 seeds = 0.2 g/seed. Seed rate = 200,000 × 0.2 g = 40,000 g/ha = 40 kg/ha, matching option (D). A common error (option B, 10) comes from inverting row and seed spacing or mixing up g/kg conversion.

subtopic: functional requirements, principles of working, construction and operation of ... equipment for ... sowing ...; calculation of performance parameters
question: The metering mechanism of a seed drill is driven by the ground wheels at a velocity ratio of 1:2. When forward speed of the seed drill is increased from 3.0 to 3.45 km h⁻¹, the seed rate would
solution: Since the metering mechanism is ground-wheel driven, the number of rotations of the metering shaft (and hence seeds dropped) per unit distance travelled is fixed by the gear/velocity ratio, independent of forward speed — both seed drop rate and ground speed scale together. Seed rate is normally expressed per unit area (kg/ha or seeds/ha), which depends only on the fixed metering-to-wheel ratio and row spacing, not on how fast the drill is pulled. So increasing forward speed changes the time taken to cover the field but not the seed rate per hectare — it remains the same, option (D). This is the key advantage of ground-wheel-driven (as opposed to engine/PTO-driven) metering: rate is self-compensating for speed changes.

subtopic: Soil tillage; forces acting on a tillage tool; hitch systems and hitching of tillage implements; functional requirements, principles of working, construction and operation of ...equipment for tillage...
question: The rear furrow wheel in a tractor mounted disc plough is provided to (A) reduce the frictional power loss (B) maintain the uniform depth of cut (C) reduce the side draft (D) improve the penetration of the plough

options.B: maintain the uniform depth of cut
options.D: improve the penetration of the plough

solution: A disc plough, unlike a mouldboard plough, generates a significant lateral (side) force due to the disc's concave, angled working surface. The rear furrow wheel is set to run against the furrow wall and take up this lateral thrust, preventing the plough (and tractor) from being pushed sideways — i.e., it counteracts/reduces the side draft. Answer: (C).

subtopic: “…cost analysis of implements and tractors, equipment for precision agriculture.”
question: The purchase price of a tractor is Rs. 5.0 lakh. Considering the constant rate of depreciation as 0.2 in declining balance method, the value of the tractor at the end of 4th year in lakh will be __________.
solution:
• Declining balance method: Value after n years = P(1–d)^n, where P = purchase price, d = depreciation rate.
• Value = 5.0 × (1–0.2)^4 = 5.0 × (0.8)^4 = 5.0 × 0.4096 = 2.048 lakh.

subtopic: “…functional requirements, principles of working, construction and operation of…spraying…”
question: The pump used in high pressure orchard sprayer is
solution:
• Orchard sprayers must deliver a fine, high-velocity spray to reach tall canopies, which requires high discharge pressure (commonly 20–40 kg/cm² or more).
• Centrifugal, rotary and turbine pumps are low-to-medium pressure, high-volume devices — pressure output is limited by impeller tip speed and cannot economically reach the high pressures orchard sprayers need.
• A plunger-type (piston) positive-displacement pump generates high pressure nearly independent of flow rate, which is why it is the standard choice for high-pressure orchard/air-blast sprayers.
• Final Answer: (C) Plunger type positive displacement pump

subtopic: “…harvesting and threshing, calculation of performance parameters – field capacity, efficiency, performance index, application rate and losses…”
question: If the Reel Speed Index of a grain combine is more than 1.5, it will increase
solution:
• Reel Speed Index (RSI) = peripheral speed of reel / forward speed of the combine.
• An RSI close to 1.0–1.5 gently strips the crop into the cutter bar. When RSI exceeds about 1.5, the reel bats strike the crop head too fast relative to machine travel, knocking grain out of the head before it is cut and gathered.
• This mechanical over-striking of the standing crop is the direct cause of increased shatter (pre-harvest) loss at the header, distinct from cylinder loss (threshing) or straw-walker loss (separation), which occur further downstream in the machine.
• Final Answer: (B) Shatter loss

subtopic: ... fuels and combustion
question: As compared to diesel, the heating value and exhaust emissions such as CO, CO₂ and smoke density of biodiesel when used in compression ignition engine are
solution: Biodiesel has a lower calorific/heating value than diesel (≈37–40 MJ/kg vs ≈45 MJ/kg) due to its oxygen content, but that same oxygen content promotes more complete combustion, so CO, CO₂ and smoke/particulate emissions are lower. Answer: Lower and lower respectively.

subtopic: ... human engineering and safety considerations in design of tractor and agricultural implements
question: In a tractor cab, the temperature comfort zone for the tractor operator is between
solution: Human-engineering standards for operator thermal comfort in a cab place the comfort band at approximately 18–24 °C, i.e. 291–297 K. This is a standard-fact question from ergonomics/human-engineering literature; the other ranges are shifted outside the accepted comfort band.

subtopic: ... lubricants and their properties
question: A lubricating oil with high viscosity index is desirable for tractor engine due to

options.A: More variation of viscosity with temperature
options.B: Less variation of viscosity with temperature

solution: Viscosity Index (VI) is a measure of how much an oil's viscosity changes with temperature. A high-VI oil maintains nearly constant viscosity across the engine's operating temperature range — desirable so lubrication is adequate both cold and hot. Answer: less variation of viscosity with temperature. Options (C)/(D) are unrelated properties (pour/cloud point relate to low-temperature flow, not VI).

subtopic: Thermodynamic principles of I.C. engines; I.C. engine cycles; engine components; fuels and combustion; ... calculation of power, torque, fuel consumption, heat load and power losses.
question:
Farm Power: Thermodynamic principles of I.C. engines; I.C. engine cycles; engine components; fuels and combustion; ... calculation of power, torque, fuel consumption, heat load and power losses.
MCQ — 1 mark
In a diesel engine with variable compression ratio, the initial compression ratio is 16:1. The ratio of specific heats is 1.4. For the same cut-off ratio of 4.0, if the compression ratio is increased by 25%, the air standard thermal efficiency of the engine will be
solution: Diesel-cycle air-standard efficiency: η = 1 − (1/r^(γ-1))·[(ρ^γ − 1)/(γ(ρ−1))], with cut-off ratio ρ=4.0, γ=1.4. For r₁=16: η₁ = 1 − (1/16^0.4)·[(4^1.4−1)/(1.4×3)] = 1 − 0.3305×0.6811×... = 0.5315 (53.15%). For r₂ = 16×1.25 = 20: η₂ = 1 − (1/20^0.4)·[same bracket] = 0.5715 (57.15%). η₂ − η₁ = 0.5715 − 0.5315 = 0.0400 → a 4.0 percentage-point increase, matching option (D). (Read as a relative increase, (η₂−η₁)/η₁ ≈ 7.5%, which is not among the options — the paper intends the absolute percentage-point change.)

subtopic: “Thermodynamic principles of I.C. engines; I.C. engine cycles…”
question: Air temperature at the beginning of adiabatic compression in an IC engine is 27 °C and the engine compression ratio is 16:1. The temperature of air at the end of the compression in °C will be __________.

subtopic: “…fuels and combustion; lubricants and their properties…”
question: A diesel fuel has same ignition delay as that of blend of two reference fuels namely 56% n-cetane and 44% hepta-methylnonane. The cetane number of the diesel fuel is __________.
solution:
• Cetane number of a reference blend = (%n-cetane × 100) + (%HMN × 15), since by definition n-cetane has CN = 100 and heptamethylnonane (HMN) has CN = 15.
• CN = 0.56 × 100 + 0.44 × 15 = 56 + 6.6 = 62.6.

subtopic: fuel, cooling, lubrication, ignition, electrical, intake and exhaust
question: The type of pump used in the forced water cooling system of a tractor engine is:
solution: Official Verified Key: B

section: Section 4: Soil and Water Conservation Engineering
question: While deriving the Chezy formula for uniform flow, it is assumed that there is a balance between
solution: In uniform flow (constant depth and velocity along the channel), the component of gravity along the channel bed exactly balances the frictional (boundary shear) resistance — there is no net acceleration, so inertial forces do not enter the balance. This gravity–friction equilibrium is exactly what the Chezy formula, V = C√(RS), expresses.

section: Section 4: Soil and Water Conservation Engineering
subtopic: dimensional analysis – concepts of geometric dimensionless numbers
question: Milk is agitated in a tank with a rotating impeller. For this system: X = P/(ρN³D⁵), Y = D²Nρ/μ, Z = DN²/g, where P = power imparted by the impeller to the fluid, N = rate of rotation, D = impeller diameter, g = acceleration due to gravity, ρ = fluid density, μ = fluid viscosity. The X, Y, Z are

options.A: X = Grashof number, Y = Power number, Z = Reynolds number
options.B: X = Power number, Y = Reynolds number, Z = Froude number
options.C: X = Reynolds number, Y = Froude number, Z = Grashof number
options.D: X = Froude number, Y = Grashof number, Z = Power number

solution: X = P/(ρN³D⁵) is the classical Power number (Np), a dimensionless group relating impeller power draw to rotational speed, density and diameter — standard in mixing-vessel design. Y = D²Nρ/μ is the (rotational) Reynolds number, Re = ρND²/μ, comparing inertial to viscous forces for a rotating impeller. Z = DN²/g is the Froude number, Fr = N²D/g, comparing inertial to gravitational forces (relevant to free-surface vortexing in agitated tanks). This matches option (B).

section: Section 4: Soil and Water Conservation Engineering
subtopic: Ideal and real fluids, properties of fluids
question: The viscosity of a newtonian fluid depends primarily on X and to a lesser degree on Y. X and Y are

options.D: X = roughness of the surface across which the fluid flows, Y = flow velocity

solution: Dynamic viscosity of a Newtonian fluid is, by definition, a property of the fluid itself (a function of its molecular structure/intermolecular forces) and is essentially independent of the flow field — it does not depend on velocity or surface roughness at all. It is strongly dependent on temperature (viscosity drops sharply with rising temperature for liquids, rises for gases) and only weakly dependent on pressure (significant only at very high pressures). This matches option (C): X = temperature (primary), Y = pressure (secondary).

section: Section 4: Soil and Water Conservation Engineering
subtopic: Ideal and real fluids, properties of fluids; continuity equation, kinematics and dynamics of flow
question: If the density of a fluid changes from point to point in a flow region, the flow is called
solution: Flow classifications are defined along different axes: steady/unsteady refers to whether properties change with time at a point; uniform/non-uniform refers to whether velocity changes with position at a given instant; and compressible/incompressible refers specifically to whether fluid density varies within the flow field. Since the question describes density varying from point to point (a spatial density variation — the hallmark property that distinguishes compressible from incompressible flow analysis), the correct classification is compressible flow, option (D). Non-uniform flow (C) is the classic distractor here because it also concerns spatial variation, but it is defined in terms of velocity, not density.

section: Section 4: Soil and Water Conservation Engineering
subtopic: “flow in open channels, dimensional analysis”
question:
The correct conditions for which the hydraulically efficient rectangular channel will deliver maximum discharge are
P – depth of water is equal to half the breadth of channel
Q – depth of water is equal to breadth of channel
R – depth of water is equal to twice the breadth of channel
S – hydraulic radius is equal to half the depth of water
solution: For the hydraulically most efficient (best) rectangular channel section, standard open-channel-hydraulics theory gives: depth y = b/2 (i.e. breadth b = 2y — statement P), and the hydraulic radius R = y/2, i.e. R equals half the depth of flow (statement S). So the correct pair is P and S → option (C). Statements Q and R use the opposite (breadth-to-depth) ratio and are the classic distractors for this well-known result.

question: The dimensionless number in heat transfer corresponding to Sherwood Number in mass transfer is
solution: Sherwood number Sh = k_c·L/D_AB (dimensionless convective mass-transfer coefficient) is the direct mass-transfer analogue of the Nusselt number Nu = h·L/k (dimensionless convective heat-transfer coefficient). Schmidt number is the mass-transfer analogue of Prandtl number, not Nusselt — a common distractor pairing.

question: The interrelationship between thermal conductivity, dynamic viscosity and temperature of gas can be described as

options.A: dynamic viscosity and thermal conductivity decrease as temperature increases
options.B: dynamic viscosity decreases and thermal conductivity increases as temperature increases
options.C: dynamic viscosity and thermal conductivity decrease as temperature decreases
options.D: dynamic viscosity and thermal conductivity increase as temperature decreases

solution: By kinetic theory of gases, both viscosity and thermal conductivity arise from molecular momentum/energy exchange, which intensifies with molecular speed — so both properties increase with temperature for a gas (opposite of liquids). Equivalently, both decrease as temperature decreases, which is option (C).

subtopic: diffusive and convective mass transfer
question: If ν is the kinematic viscosity of air–water vapour mixture and D_AB is the mass diffusivity of water vapour in air, the ratio ν/D_AB is known as:
solution: Official Verified Key: C

section: Section 4: Soil and Water Conservation Engineering
question: An effective rainfall of 20 mm h⁻¹ occurs for 2 hours in a catchment. The time of concentration of the catchment is 1.5 hour. The peak of the resulting direct runoff hydrograph, in mm h⁻¹, is
solution: Peak (equilibrium) discharge is reached once the entire catchment is contributing simultaneously, i.e. once rainfall has lasted at least one time of concentration (tc = 1.5 h). Since the storm duration (2 h) exceeds tc, the catchment reaches full contribution and the runoff hydrograph rises to, and holds at, the rainfall excess rate itself, 20 mm h⁻¹, before receding once rainfall stops.

section: Section 4: Soil and Water Conservation Engineering
subtopic: flood routing, hydrological reservoir and channel routing
question: The wedge storage in a river reach during the passage of a flood wave is
solution: In channel (Muskingum-type) flood routing, total storage in a reach is split into prism storage (a function of outflow alone) and wedge storage (the extra storage caused by the difference between inflow and outflow along the reach, which gives the water surface a wedge shape). During the rising limb of a flood, inflow exceeds outflow, so the wedge is positive (water is being added on top of the prism, sloping upward toward the upstream end) — option (A). During the falling limb, outflow exceeds inflow and the wedge becomes negative.

section: Section 4: Soil and Water Conservation Engineering
subtopic: “analysis of precipitation data”
question: The normal annual rainfall for 5 rain gauge stations A, B, C, D, E were 112.7, 120.4, 118.3, 125.2 and 110.6 cm respectively. In a particular year station C failed; A, B, D, E recorded 114.9, 118.3, 122.6 and 114.5 cm. The estimated rainfall at station C in cm was ______
solution: Using the Normal Ratio Method (since normal annual rainfall values of the stations differ by more than 10% from each other): P_C = (N_C/M)×Σ(P_i/N_i) for the M=4 index stations, where N is normal annual rainfall and P is the recorded rainfall in the deficient year. P_C = (118.3/4)×[(114.9/112.7)+(118.3/120.4)+(122.6/125.2)+(114.5/110.6)] = 29.575×[1.0195+0.9826+0.9792+1.0353] = 29.575×4.0166 = 118.79 cm, within the accepted band 118.5–119.0.

topic: Irrigation Water Conveyance and Application Methods
question: A cross regulator is usually provided

options.A: at the head of the off-taking channel
options.B: in the main channel upstream of the off-taking channel
options.C: in the main channel downstream of the off-taking channel
options.D: in the watercourse to regulate the outlets

solution: A cross regulator spans the main/parent channel just downstream of an off-take, so that when it is partially closed it backs up (raises) the water level in the main channel at the off-take point, forcing more discharge into the distributary. A head regulator, not a cross regulator, sits at the head of the off-taking channel itself (A is a distractor naming the wrong structure).

subtopic: Eigen values and Eigen vectors, solutions of linear equations
question:
2
Eigenvalues of the matrix [[2,1],[2,3]] are
solution: Characteristic equation: λ² − (trace)λ + det = 0 → λ² − 5λ + (6−2) = λ² − 5λ + 4 = 0 → (λ−1)(λ−4) = 0 → λ = 1, 4.

subtopic: Matrices and determinants
question: A square matrix [A] will be lower triangular if and only if (a_MN represents an element of Mth row and Nth column of the matrix)
solution: In a lower-triangular matrix, all entries above the main diagonal are zero, and only entries on or below the diagonal may be non-zero. An entry a_MN lies above the diagonal precisely when its column index exceeds its row index, i.e. N > M. Hence the defining condition is a_MN = 0 for N > M, which is option (A). Option (D) wrongly requires those above-diagonal entries to be non-zero (that would describe an upper triangular matrix's complement), and (B)/(C) swap the row–column inequality.

subtopic: Matrices and determinants
question: The matrix [[0, 2, -3], [-2, 0, 4], [3, -4, 0]] is:
solution: Official Verified Key: C

subtopic: Matrices and determinants, linear and orthogonal transformations, Caley Hamilton theorem; Eigen values and Eigen vectors, solutions of linear equations.
question:
Linear Algebra: Matrices and determinants, linear and orthogonal transformations, Caley Hamilton theorem; Eigen values and Eigen vectors, solutions of linear equations.
MCQ — 1 mark
Inverse of the matrix (2 3; 2 1) is
solution: For A = [[2,3],[2,1]], det(A) = 2(1) - 3(2) = 2 - 6 = -4. Adjugate = [[1,-3],[-2,2]]. A^-1 = (1/det)*adj = (1/-4)*[[1,-3],[-2,2]] = [[-0.25, 0.75],[0.5, -0.5]]. This matches option (C). Option (A) has the correct magnitudes but the sign pattern of a cofactor swap is wrong; (B) and (D) come from mis-placing the off-diagonal terms during adjugate formation.

subtopic: Matrices and determinants, linear and orthogonal transformations, Caley Hamilton theorem; Eigen values and Eigen vectors, solutions of linear equations.
question: If P = A × B, where A = [[2,1],[3,0]] and B = [[1,3,0],[2,1,2]]; then P is (A) [[7,2],[9,0]] (B) [[4,7,2],[3,9,0]] (C) [[2,4],[3,9]] (D) [[2,4,7],[0,3,9]]
solution:
Standard matrix multiplication, P = A×B (2×2 times 2×3 gives 2×3):
Row 1: [2×1+1×2, 2×3+1×1, 2×0+1×2] = [4, 7, 2]
Row 2: [3×1+0×2, 3×3+0×1, 3×0+0×2] = [3, 9, 0]
P = [[4,7,2],[3,9,0]]. Answer: (B). (Verified symbolically.)

subtopic: Matrices and determinants... Eigen values and Eigen vectors, solutions of linear equations.
question: Eigenvalues of the matrix [[2,1],[3,2]] are (A) 2i (B) 2±3i (C) 2±√3i (D) 2±√3
solution: Characteristic equation: det(A−λI) = (2−λ)² − 3 = 0 ⇒ (2−λ)² = 3 ⇒ 2−λ = ±√3 ⇒ λ = 2∓√3, i.e., λ = 2±√3 (real, since discriminant of λ²−4λ+1=0 is 16−4=12>0). Answer: (D). (Verified symbolically.)

subtopic: “Eigen values and Eigen vectors, solutions of linear equations”
question: Eigen values of the matrix [[5,3],[1,4]] are
solution: Characteristic equation: det(A-λI)=0 → (5-λ)(4-λ)-3(1)=0 → λ²-9λ+17=0. Using the quadratic formula: λ = (9 ± √(81-68))/2 = (9 ± √13)/2 = (9 ± 3.606)/2. This gives λ₁ = 6.303 and λ₂ = 2.297, i.e. 2.3 and 6.3 → option (D). Option (C) is the same pair with a sign/order slip; (A) and (B) come from mis-signing the trace (9) or the discriminant.

subtopic: “Matrices and determinants, linear and orthogonal transformations, Caley Hamilton theorem; Eigen values and Eigen vectors, solutions of linear equations.”
question: Matrix [[0, 0.5, 1.5], [-0.5, 0, 2.5], [-1.5, -2.5, 0]] is a
solution:
• A matrix A is skew-symmetric if A^T = –A, i.e. a_ij = –a_ji for every i, j, and all diagonal entries are zero.
• Here a12 = 0.5 and a21 = –0.5 (=–a12); a13 = 1.5 and a31 = –1.5 (=–a13); a23 = 2.5 and a32 = –2.5 (=–a23). All diagonal entries are 0.
• Every off-diagonal pair satisfies a_ij = –a_ji, so the matrix is skew-symmetric.
• Distractor logic: it is not diagonal (off-diagonal terms are non-zero), not symmetric (a_ij ≠ a_ji), and not orthogonal (A A^T ≠ I, since a skew-symmetric matrix is orthogonal only in special cases which do not hold here).
• Final Answer: (D) Skew-symmetric matrix

subtopic: “…Eigen values and Eigen vectors, solutions of linear equations.”
question: Characteristic equation of the matrix [[2, √2], [√2, 1]] with Eigen value λ is
solution:
• For a 2×2 matrix, the characteristic equation is λ² – (trace)λ + det(A) = 0.
• Trace = 2 + 1 = 3.
• det(A) = (2)(1) – (√2)(√2) = 2 – 2 = 0.
• Characteristic equation: λ² – 3λ + 0 = 0, i.e. λ² – 3λ = 0.
• Distractor logic: (A) and (B) use an incorrect determinant (treating √2×√2 as something other than 2, or adding instead of subtracting); (D) flips the sign of the trace term.
• Final Answer: (C) λ² – 3λ = 0

subtopic: Design and selection of machine elements ... overload safety devices used in farm machinery
question: As per ASABE standards, the three-point hitch of a two-wheel drive tractor with a maximum drawbar power of 45 kW comes under the category
solution: ASABE/OECD three-point hitch categories are graded by tractor drawbar power: Category I ≈ up to 20 kW (≈25 hp drawbar/48 hp PTO band), Category II ≈ 20–45 kW, Category III ≈ 45–92 kW, Category IV ≈ above 92 kW. 45 kW falls at the top of the Category II band. Answer: Category II.

subtopic: Design and selection of machine elements – gears, pulleys, chains and sprockets and belts
question: The theoretical percentage variation in speed of a chain as it leaves an 8 teeth sprocket rotating at a uniform velocity is
solution: Chordal (polygonal) action: the chain's linear speed varies between v_max = v(pitch circle) and v_min = v·cos(180°/n). Percentage variation ≈ [1 − cos(180°/n)] × 100, with n = 8 teeth, half-angle θ = 180/8 = 22.5°. 1 − cos(22.5°) = 1 − 0.9239 = 0.0761 → ≈7.9% (matches option B within rounding of the standard chordal-action approximation). (C),(D) come from using the reciprocal/secant form of the variation formula instead.

subtopic: Basic English Grammar & Vocabulary
question:
General Aptitude
Not part of the attached AG syllabus PDF — General Aptitude (GA) is a common section administered in every GATE paper, covering Verbal Ability and Numerical/Quantitative Ability.
The fishermen, ______ the flood victims owed their lives, were rewarded by the government.
solution: The flood victims owed their lives 'to' the fishermen, so the relative pronoun must carry the preposition 'to'. Since the antecedent (fishermen) is a person, 'whom' is correct, and the preposition must be placed before it in formal written English: "to whom". (A) drops the required preposition, (B) wrongly uses 'which' for a person, (D) 'that' cannot follow a preposition in this construction. Answer: (C) to whom.

section: Section 4: Soil and Water Conservation Engineering
subtopic: Basic English Grammar & Vocabulary
question:
General Aptitude
Not part of the attached AG syllabus PDF — General Aptitude (GA) is a common section administered in every GATE paper, covering Verbal Ability and Numerical/Quantitative Ability.
Some students were not involved in the strike. If the above statement is true, which of the following conclusions is/are logically necessary?
1. Some who were involved in the strike were students.
2. No student was involved in the strike.
3. At least one student was involved in the strike.
4. Some who were not involved in the strike were students.
solution: "Some students were not involved in the strike" only asserts that at least one student was a non-participant; it says nothing about whether any student *was* involved (statements 1 and 3 are not forced), and it does not claim ALL students were uninvolved (statement 2 is too strong). The only statement that is a direct logical restatement of the given premise (commutativity of 'some') is statement 4: "Some who were not involved in the strike were students." Answer: (C) 4.

question:
General Aptitude
Not part of the attached AG syllabus PDF — General Aptitude (GA) is a common section administered in every GATE paper, covering Verbal Ability and Numerical/Quantitative Ability.
The radius as well as the height of a circular cone increases by 10%. The percentage increase in its volume is ______.
solution: Volume V = (1/3)πr²h. If r → 1.1r and h → 1.1h, V_new = (1/3)π(1.1r)²(1.1h) = 1.1³ × V = 1.331 V. Percentage increase = (1.331 − 1) × 100 = 33.1%. Distractor (A) 17.1% comes from adding percentages linearly for one factor only (2×10%+... miscalculated); (D) 72.8% would correspond to (1.1)⁶. Answer: (C) 33.1.

subtopic: Basic English Grammar & Vocabulary
question:
General Aptitude
Not part of the attached AG syllabus PDF — General Aptitude (GA) is a common section administered in every GATE paper, covering Verbal Ability and Numerical/Quantitative Ability.
Five numbers 10, 7, 5, 4 and 2 are to be arranged in a sequence left to right following:
1. No two odd or even numbers are next to each other.
2. The second number from the left is exactly half of the left-most number.
3. The middle number is exactly twice the right-most number.
Which is the second number from the right?
solution: Numbers: 10,7,5,4,2 (odd: 7,5; even: 10,4,2). Rule 1 forces strict alternation O-E-O-E-E is impossible with 3 evens/2 odds unless the pattern is E-O-E-O-E. Rule 2: position2 = position1/2, so position1 must be even and twice position2. Testing E-O-E-O-E with position1=10, position2=5 (10/2=5 ✓, both valid parities). Remaining numbers {7,4,2} fill positions 3,4,5 with position3 even, position4 odd(=7), position5 even. Rule 3: middle (position3) = 2×position5(right-most). From {4,2} for positions 3 and 5: 4=2×2 ✓, so position3=4, position5=2. Sequence: 10,5,4,7,2. Second from the right = position 4 = 7. Answer: (C) 7.

question:
General Aptitude
Not part of the attached AG syllabus PDF — General Aptitude (GA) is a common section administered in every GATE paper, covering Verbal Ability and Numerical/Quantitative Ability.
Since the last one year, after a 125 basis point reduction in repo rate by the RBI, banking institutions have been making a demand to reduce interest rates on small saving schemes. Finally, the government announced yesterday a reduction in interest rates on small saving schemes to bring them on par with fixed deposit interest rates.
Which statement can be inferred from the passage?

options.A: Whenever RBI reduces the repo rate, interest rates on small saving schemes are also reduced
options.B: Interest rates on small saving schemes are always maintained on par with fixed deposit interest rates
options.C: The government sometimes takes into consideration the demands of banking institutions before reducing interest rates on small saving schemes
options.D: A reduction in interest rates on small saving schemes follows only after a reduction in repo rate by RBI

solution: The passage describes one specific instance: banks demanded a rate cut, and the government eventually reduced the rate. This supports only a modest, hedged inference — that government *sometimes* responds to such demands — matching (C). (A) and (D) claim a universal ('whenever'/'only after') causal rule from a single instance, which is unsupported. (B) claims a permanent state ('always'), but the passage describes a one-time alignment. Answer: (C).

Two trains started at 7AM from the same point. The first travelled north at 80 km/h and the second travelled south at 100 km/h. The time at which they were 540 km apart is ______ AM.
solution: The trains move in opposite directions, so the separation rate = 80 + 100 = 180 km/h. Time to reach 540 km apart = 540/180 = 3 hours after 7 AM = 10:00 AM. Answer: (B) 10.

question:
The number of students passing or failing in an exam for a particular subject are presented in the bar chart above (Year 1: Pass 50, Fail 10; Year 2: Pass 60, Fail 5; Year 3: Pass 50, Fail 3). Students who pass the exam cannot appear for the exam again. Students who fail the exam in the first attempt must appear for the exam in the following year. Students always pass the exam in their second attempt. The number of students who took the exam for the first time in the year 2 and the year 3 respectively, are ______.
Figure (reconstruction)
solution: Year 1 is the first year, so all 60 (50 pass + 10 fail) are first-timers. The 10 who failed retake the exam in Year 2 and — since a repeater always passes on the second attempt — all 10 appear in Year 2's PASS count. Year 2 total = 60+5 = 65, of which 10 are guaranteed-pass repeaters, so first-time takers in Year 2 = 65 − 10 = 55. Of these 55 first-timers, 5 fail (matches the Year-2 fail count exactly, since repeaters cannot fail) and 50 pass. Those 5 Year-2 failures repeat in Year 3 and must pass. Year 3 total = 50+3 = 53, of which 5 are repeaters, so first-time takers in Year 3 = 53 − 5 = 48. Answer: 55 and 48 → (D).

subtopic: Logical reasoning (seating/arrangement puzzle).
question: Seven cars P, Q, R, S, T, U and V are parked in a row not necessarily in that order. The cars T and U should be parked next to each other. The cars S and V also should be parked next to each other, whereas P and Q cannot be parked next to each other. Q and S must be parked next to each other. R is parked to the immediate right of V. T is parked to the left of U. Based on the above statements, the only INCORRECT option given below is:

options.A: There are two cars parked in between Q and V.
options.B: Q and R are not parked together.
options.C: V is the only car parked in between S and R.
options.D: Car P is parked at the extreme end.

solution:
Since Q–S are adjacent and S–V are adjacent, S sits between Q and V; and since R is immediately right of V, the fixed sub-block is Q-S-V-R (only one car, S, lies between Q and V — so C is true and A, which claims two cars lie between Q and V, is impossible). With T immediately left of U forming block T-U, and P a single unit, one valid full arrangement satisfying every remaining constraint (P not adjacent to Q) is T U Q S V R P: here Q and R (positions 3 and 6) are not adjacent (B holds), V lies strictly between S and R (C holds), and P sits at the extreme right end (D holds). Only statement (A) — "two cars between Q and V" — is always false, since exactly one car (S) separates them. Hence (A) is the only incorrect statement.

subtopic: Mensuration (area of similar figures).
question: In the figure shown above (a 10 cm × 10 cm square with successively smaller squares each formed by joining the midpoints of the sides of the next larger square, the innermost being shaded grey), each inside square is formed by joining the midpoints of the sides of the next larger square. The area of the smallest square (shaded) as shown, in cm², is:
solution: Joining the midpoints of a square's sides produces a new (rotated) square whose area is exactly HALF the area of the parent square (side of new square = (side/√2), so area = side²/2). Starting from the outer 10 cm × 10 cm square (area = 100 cm²), each successive nested square halves the area: 100 → 50 → 25 → 12.5 → 6.25 → 3.125 cm². The figure shows the outer square followed by four more nested squares down to the shaded one (five halving steps in total), giving 100 × (1/2)^5 = 3.125 cm², matching option (C).

subtopic: Number properties / divisibility.
question: Which one of the following numbers is exactly divisible by (11^13 + 1)?
solution: Let x = 11. Since x ≡ −1 (mod x^13 + 1), any even power of x^13 is ≡ 1 (mod x^13+1). x^52 = (x^13)^4 ≡ (−1)^4 = 1 (mod x^13+1), so x^52 − 1 ≡ 0 — divisible. Checking distractors: x^26 = (x^13)^2 ≡ 1, so x^26+1 ≡ 2 (not divisible, rules out A). x^33 is not an integer multiple of 13 so no clean reduction applies (rules out B). x^39=(x^13)^3≡(−1)^3=−1, so x^39−1≡−2 (not divisible, rules out C). Hence (D) is correct.

subtopic: probability (Bayes' theorem)
question: 10% of the population in a town is HIV+. A new diagnostic kit for HIV detection is available; this kit correctly identifies HIV+ individuals 95% of the time, and HIV− individuals 89% of the time. A particular patient is tested using this kit and is found to be positive. The probability that the individual is actually positive is _______
solution:
By Bayes' theorem: P(HIV+|Test+) = P(Test+|HIV+)·P(HIV+) / P(Test+).
P(Test+|HIV+) = 0.95, P(HIV+) = 0.10 → numerator = 0.095.
P(Test+|HIV−) = 1 − 0.89 = 0.11 (false-positive rate), P(HIV−) = 0.90 → 0.90×0.11 = 0.099.
P(Test+) = 0.095 + 0.099 = 0.194.
P(HIV+|Test+) = 0.095 / 0.194 = 0.4897, within the accepted range 0.48–0.49.

subtopic: Geometry (Mutually Tangent Circles)
question:
Circles C₁, C₂, and C₃, with centres O₁, O₂, and O₃, and radii r₁, r₂, and r₃ respectively, touch each other as shown in the figure. Given r₁ = 2 cm, r₂ = 1 cm and the angle ∠O₁O₃O₂ = 90°, r₃ = _____ cm.

Figure Q.10 — three mutually touching circles
solution:
For circles touching externally, the distance between centres equals the sum of the radii:
O₁O₃ = r₁ + r₃ = 2 + r₃
O₂O₃ = r₂ + r₃ = 1 + r₃
O₁O₂ = r₁ + r₂ = 3
Since ∠O₁O₃O₂ = 90°, triangle O₁O₃O₂ is right-angled at O₃, so by Pythagoras:
(2 + r₃)² + (1 + r₃)² = 3²
(4 + 4r₃ + r₃²) + (1 + 2r₃ + r₃²) = 9
2r₃² + 6r₃ − 4 = 0
r₃² + 3r₃ − 2 = 0
r₃ = [−3 ± √(9 + 8)]/2 = ½(−3 ± √17)
Radius must be positive ⇒ r₃ = ½(−3 + √17) ≈ 0.562 cm.

subtopic: Logarithms and Algebraic Identities
question: For positive non-zero real variables p and q, if log(p² + q²) = log p + log q + 2 log 3, then the value of (p⁴ + q⁴)/(p²q²) is
solution:
Step 1 — remove the logarithms.
log(p² + q²) = log p + log q + 2 log 3 = log(p · q · 3²) = log(9pq)
⇒ p² + q² = 9pq
Step 2 — build the required expression. Square both sides:
(p² + q²)² = (9pq)²
p⁴ + 2p²q² + q⁴ = 81p²q²
p⁴ + q⁴ = 79p²q²
Step 3 — divide:
(p⁴ + q⁴)/(p²q²) = 79
Trap: forgetting to subtract the cross term 2p²q² gives 81 — option (B).

subtopic: Mensuration (Solids)
question:
A rectangular paper sheet of dimensions 54 cm × 4 cm is taken. The two longer edges of the sheet are joined together to create a cylindrical tube. A cube whose surface area is equal to the area of the sheet is also taken.
Then, the ratio of the volume of the cylindrical tube to the volume of the cube is
solution:
Step 1 — the cylinder. Joining the two longer edges (each 54 cm) means those edges become the seam running along the tube’s length. Therefore:
Height of cylinder, h = 54 cm
Circumference = the shorter side = 4 cm ⇒ 2πr = 4 ⇒ r = 2/π cm
Volume of cylinder = πr²h = π × (2/π)² × 54 = π × (4/π²) × 54 = 216/π cm³
Step 2 — the cube. Area of the sheet = 54 × 4 = 216 cm²
Surface area of cube = 6a² = 216 ⇒ a² = 36 ⇒ a = 6 cm
Volume of cube = 6³ = 216 cm³
Step 3 — ratio:
(216/π)/216 = 1/π

subtopic: Mensuration and geometry
question:
GA Q.3
For 0 ≤ x ≤ 2π, sin x and cos x are both decreasing functions in the interval ________.
solution:
sin x decreases where cos x < 0, i.e. on (π/2, 3π/2).
cos x decreases where sin x > 0, i.e. on (0, π).
Intersection of (π/2, 3π/2) and (0, π) = (π/2, π).

subtopic: Mensuration and geometry
question:
GA Q.4
The area of an equilateral triangle is √3. What is the perimeter of the triangle?
solution:
Area of an equilateral triangle of side a: A = (√3/4)a².
(√3/4)a² = √3 ⇒ a² = 4 ⇒ a = 2 units.
Perimeter = 3a = 3 × 2 = 6 units.
Distractor (A) = a itself; (B) mistakes the formula as (√3/2)a².

subtopic: Mensuration and geometry
question:
GA Q.5
Arrange the following three-dimensional objects in the descending order of their volumes:
(i) A cuboid with dimensions 10 cm, 8 cm and 6 cm
(ii) A cube of side 8 cm
(iii) A cylinder with base radius 7 cm and height 7 cm
(iv) A sphere of radius 7 cm
solution:
Cuboid: V = 10 × 8 × 6 = 480 cm³.
Cube: V = 8³ = 512 cm³.
Cylinder: V = πr²h = (22/7)(7²)(7) = 1078 cm³.
Sphere: V = (4/3)πr³ = (4/3)(22/7)(343) = 1437.3 cm³.
Descending order: sphere > cylinder > cube > cuboid ⇒ (iv), (iii), (ii), (i).

subtopic: Numerical computation and estimation: ratios, percentages, powers, exponents and logarithms, permutations and combinations, and series
question:
GA Q.6
An automobile travels from city A to city B and returns to city A by the same route. The speed of the vehicle during the onward and return journeys were constant at 60 km/h and 90 km/h, respectively. What is the average speed in km/h for the entire journey?
solution:
Equal distances ⇒ average speed is the harmonic mean of the two speeds.
V_avg = 2v₁v₂/(v₁+v₂) = 2 × 60 × 90 / (60+90) = 10800/150 = 72 km/h.
Distractor (D) 75 is the arithmetic mean (60+90)/2 — the classic error, valid only for equal times, not equal distances.

subtopic: Numerical computation and estimation: ratios, percentages, powers, exponents and logarithms, permutations and combinations, and series
question:
GA Q.7
A set of 4 parallel lines intersect with another set of 5 parallel lines. How many parallelograms are formed?
solution:
A parallelogram needs 2 lines from the first family and 2 from the second.
N = C(4,2) × C(5,2) = 6 × 10 = 60.
Distractor (A) 20 = 4 × 5, i.e. counting intersection points instead of parallelograms.

subtopic: Numerical computation and estimation: ratios, percentages, powers, exponents and logarithms, permutations and combinations, and series
question:
GA Q.8
To pass a test, a candidate needs to answer at least 2 out of 3 questions correctly. A total of 6,30,000 candidates appeared for the test. Question A was correctly answered by 3,30,000 candidates. Question B was answered correctly by 2,50,000 candidates. Question C was answered correctly by 2,60,000 candidates. Both questions A and B were answered correctly by 1,00,000 candidates. Both questions B and C were answered correctly by 90,000 candidates. Both questions A and C were answered correctly by 80,000 candidates. If the number of students answering all questions correctly is the same as the number answering none, how many candidates failed to clear the test?
solution:
Work in thousands. Let x = |A∩B∩C| = number answering none.
Inclusion–exclusion: |A∪B∪C| = 330 + 250 + 260 − 100 − 90 − 80 + x = 570 + x.
Total = |A∪B∪C| + none ⇒ 630 = (570 + x) + x ⇒ x = 30 (i.e. 30,000).
Exactly two correct = (100−30) + (90−30) + (80−30) = 70 + 60 + 50 = 180.
Passed = exactly two + all three = 180 + 30 = 210 ⇒ 2,10,000.
Failed = 630 − 210 = 420 ⇒ 4,20,000.
Distractor (C) 3,90,000 arises from forgetting to subtract the all-three group from each pairwise count.

subtopic: Numerical computation and estimation: ratios, percentages, powers, exponents and logarithms, permutations and combinations, and series
question:
GA Q.9
If x² + x − 1 = 0, what is the value of x⁴ + 1/x⁴ ?
solution:
Divide x² + x − 1 = 0 by x: x + 1 − 1/x = 0 ⇒ x − 1/x = −1.
x² + 1/x² = (x − 1/x)² + 2 = 1 + 2 = 3.
x⁴ + 1/x⁴ = (x² + 1/x²)² − 2 = 9 − 2 = 7.
Distractor (D) 9 is (x² + 1/x²)² without subtracting 2.

subtopic: Ratio and Percentage
question: The number of coins of ₹1, ₹5, and ₹10 denominations that a person has are in the ratio 5:3:13. Of the total amount, the percentage of money in ₹5 coins is
solution:
Let the numbers of coins be 5x, 3x and 13x.
Value of each denomination:
₹1 coins: 5x × 1 = 5x
₹5 coins: 3x × 5 = 15x
₹10 coins: 13x × 10 = 130x
Total amount = 5x + 15x + 130x = 150x
Percentage in ₹5 coins = (15x/150x) × 100 = 10%
Trap: option (B) 14 2/7 % is the percentage of the number of coins (3/21), not of the money.

subtopic: Ratio and Proportion / Algebra
question: If two distinct non-zero real variables x and y are such that (x + y) is proportional to (x − y) then the value of x/y

options.B: depends only on x and not on y
options.C: depends only on y and not on x

solution:
Proportionality means there exists a constant k such that:
x + y = k(x − y)
Divide throughout by y (y ≠ 0), and let t = x/y:
t + 1 = k(t − 1)
t + 1 = kt − k
t(1 − k) = −(1 + k)
t = (1 + k)/(k − 1)
The right-hand side contains only the proportionality constant k. Therefore x/y is itself a constant, independent of the individual values of x and y.

subtopic: Set Theory / Venn Diagrams
question:
In a population, patients who have high cholesterol also have high blood-pressure (BP). Some patients with high BP also have diabetes. There are no patients who have both high cholesterol and diabetes. Furthermore,
1. the total number of patients with at least one of these conditions is 75,
2. the number of patients with high cholesterol is 10,
3. the number of patients with high BP is 45, and
4. the number of patients with only high BP and no other conditions is 20.
Then the number of patients who have both diabetes and high BP is _______
solution:
From the conditions: Cholesterol set C ⊂ BP set B, and C ∩ Diabetes D = ∅.
The BP set therefore splits into exactly three disjoint parts:
n(B) = (only BP) + (BP ∩ C) + (BP ∩ D)
45 = 20 + 10 + x
x = 15
Consistency check: patients with at least one condition = n(B) + (diabetes only) = 45 + 30 = 75 ✔ (so 30 patients have diabetes alone).

subtopic: Statistics (Median)
question:
Consider the following sample of numbers: 9, 18, 11, 14, 15, 17, 10, 69, 11, 13
The median of the sample is
solution:
Step 1 — arrange in ascending order:
9, 10, 11, 11, 13, 14, 15, 17, 18, 69
Step 2 — count: n = 10 (even). The median is the average of the 5ᵗʰ and 6ᵗʰ values:
Median = (13 + 14)/2 = 13.5
Note: the mean is 18.7 — option (D) — deliberately placed as a distractor. The outlier 69 inflates the mean but leaves the median unaffected, which is precisely why the median is preferred for skewed data.

subtopic: Numerical Computation
question: The coefficient of x⁴ in the polynomial (x − 1)³(x − 2)³ is equal to _______. (A) 33 (B) −3 (C) 30 (D) 21
solution:
Expand (x−1)³(x−2)³ = [(x−1)(x−2)]³ = (x²−3x+2)³. Using the multinomial expansion of (x²−3x+2)³, the x⁴ term arises from choosing exponents (a,b,c) on (x²)^a(−3x)^b(2)^c with a+b+c=3 and 2a+b=4. Valid combinations: (a,b,c)=(2,0,1) and (1,2,0).
• (2,0,1): coefficient = 3!/(2!0!1!) × 1² × 1 × 2 = 3×2 = 6
• (1,2,0): coefficient = 3!/(1!2!0!) × 1 × (−3)² × 1 = 3×9 = 27
Total coefficient of x⁴ = 6+27 = 33. Answer: (A) 33. (Verified independently by symbolic expansion.)

topic: Quantitative Aptitude – arithmetic operations / functional notation
question:
4
General Aptitude
Quantitative Aptitude – arithmetic operations / functional notation
MCQ — 1 mark
Operators □, ◇ and → are defined by: a□b = (a−b)/(a+b); a◇b = (a+b)/(a−b); a→b = ab.
Find the value of (66 □ 6) → (66 ◇ 6).
solution:
First evaluate the two bracketed terms using the given definitions:
66 □ 6 = (66−6)/(66+6) = 60/72 = 5/6.
66 ◇ 6 = (66+6)/(66−6) = 72/60 = 6/5.
Now apply a→b = ab on these results: (5/6) → (6/5) = (5/6)×(6/5) = 1. Note that ◇ is exactly the reciprocal of □ for the same operand pair, so their product under → always equals 1 — recognising this shortcut avoids arithmetic errors. Hence (C) is correct.

question:
5
General Aptitude
Quantitative Aptitude – logarithms
MCQ — 1 mark
If logₓ(5/7) = −1/3, then the value of x is
solution: By definition of logarithm, logₓ(5/7) = −1/3 means x^(−1/3) = 5/7, i.e. x^(1/3) = 7/5. Cubing both sides: x = (7/5)³ = 343/125. Options (C) and (D) are negative and can be eliminated immediately because a positive base raised to any real power cannot give a negative result equal to 5/7 in the defining equation; (B) is the reciprocal of the correct answer, a common inversion error from mishandling the negative exponent. Hence (A) 343/125 is correct.

subtopic: Ratios & Percentages
question: To construct a wall, sand and cement are mixed in the ratio of 3:1. The cost of sand and that of cement are in the ratio of 1:2. If the total cost of sand and cement to construct the wall is 1000 rupees, then what is the cost (in rupees) of cement used? (A) 400 (B) 600 (C) 800 (D) 200
solution: Let the quantity of sand = 3k, cement = k (mixing ratio 3:1). Let unit cost of sand = c, unit cost of cement = 2c (cost ratio 1:2). Cost of sand = 3k×c = 3kc; cost of cement = k×2c = 2kc. Total cost = 3kc+2kc = 5kc = 1000 ⇒ kc = 200. Cost of cement = 2kc = 400. Answer: (A) 400. *Distractor note:* (C) 800 results from mixing up which ratio (mixing vs cost) applies to which quantity.

question: The importance of sleep is often overlooked by students when they are preparing for exams. Research has consistently shown that sleep deprivation greatly reduces the ability to recall the material learnt. Hence, cutting down on sleep to study longer hours can be counterproductive. Which one of the following statements is the CORRECT inference from the above passage?

options.A: Sleeping well alone is enough to prepare for an exam. Studying has lesser benefit.
options.B: Students are efficient and are not wrong in thinking that sleep is a waste of time.
options.C: If a student is extremely well prepared for an exam, he needs little or no sleep.
options.D: To do well in an exam, adequate sleep must be part of the preparation.

solution: The passage states sleep deprivation reduces recall, so cutting sleep to study more is counterproductive — i.e., sleep is a necessary component of effective exam preparation, not a substitute for study (rules out A, which over-extends the claim) nor irrelevant (rules out B, C, which contradict the passage directly).
